title: Quenched Thermodynamics from Ancilla-Assisted Imaginary-Time Evolution
abstract: Quenched thermodynamics combines the equilibrium physics of fixed coupling configurations with a prescribed distribution of disorder. Problems related to quenched thermodynamics are generally intractable to approximate. We provide a quantum algorithm to calculate quenched disorder averages for the transverse-field Ising model, whose coupling configurations are organized into gauge classes. We show how to estimate these averages by preparing approximate Gibbs states through ancilla-assisted imaginary-time evolution. At each measurement, the ancilla record identifies the gauge class to which the energy estimate contributes.   We validate our framework through an open $3\times3$ lattice. A one-step circuit resolves all sixteen flux classes, and a finite-shot calculation estimates the quenched energy for independently distributed bond signs. Thermodynamic integration extends the reconstruction to a quenched free-energy estimate, while comparison with exact diagonalization identifies the finite-step approximation as the dominant source of error. This use of the measurement record provides access to the thermodynamics of frustrated spin systems with a disorder distribution chosen independently of the circuit's sampling frequencies.
summary: This paper presents a quantum algorithm to calculate quenched disorder averages for models like the transverse-field Ising model. It uses ancilla-assisted imaginary-time evolution, where the measurement record helps classify the disorder configuration into gauge classes. This allows for the estimation of quenched free energies, providing access to complex disordered systems otherwise inaccessible to current methods.
main_problem: The paper addresses the generally intractable problem of calculating quenched disorder averages in quantum systems, particularly for the transverse-field Ising model.
main_result: They successfully provide a quantum algorithm to estimate these disorder averages and free energies by leveraging ancilla-assisted imaginary-time evolution.
method: The core method involves preparing approximate Gibbs states via imaginary-time evolution and using the measurement record to identify and weight contributions from distinct gauge classes.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the transverse-field Ising model on a lattice, whose disorder is encoded in the signs of the coupling constants ($s_\ell(u,v)$). The physics is characterized by gauge classes determined by the magnetic flux ($\Phi$) around lattice loops.
key_observables: Quenched disorder averages, quenched free energy ($F( eta)$), class-conditioned energy estimates ($\langle H(\omega) angle_ eta$), and the difference between quenched and annealed free energies.

main_assumptions: The method relies on the measurement record accurately identifying the gauge class, and approximations are made regarding the finite-step nature of the imaginary-time evolution circuit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the process of identifying flux classes via plaquette products, comparing calculated class energies (ED vs. circuit estimates), and showing the reconstruction of quenched energy on open lattices.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework for quenched averages, details the quantum algorithmic implementation using ancilla-assisted evolution, validates the method on small lattices, and compares the resulting quenched free energy estimates against exact diagonalization results.
why_interesting: The technique provides a powerful quantum simulation tool to probe complex, disordered many-body physics (like spin glasses) that are analytically or numerically intractable, bridging quantum computation with advanced statistical mechanics.
